To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mucus transport in trachea is maximum when the mucus layer thickness is about 50% of the total depth of mucus layer and serous layer and the mucus viscosity is 0.01 poise.

the effect of mucus visco-elasticity is to decrease the mucus transport, the effect of mocus porosity is to increase the mucus transport and the effect of serous layer porosity is to decrease the mucous transport.
the mucus transport is enhanced as the pressure drop and porosity of mucus increase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model that is based on the two-layer fluid model for the mucus transport in human trachea.

the steady state mucus transport in the trachea and it is shown that the mucus transport is a function of mucus viscosity and porosity parameter, pressure gradient and the velocity generated by the cilia tips.

the steady state transport of the mucus layer in a cylindrical two fluid model of the human tracheal wall, where the mucus is treated as a viscoelastic fluid, and the ciliary beating is modeled as a prescribed shear stress at the interface of mucus layer and serous sub-layer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mucus transport is a function of the pressure gradient, the velocity generated due to cilia tips, the porosity parameter and the thickness of serous sub-layer, but not the viscosities of mucus or serous layer fluids.

the transport of the mucus layer increases with increase in pressure drop, velocity generated due to cilia tips and the porosity parameter and it decreases with an increase in the viscosity of mucus and serous fluid layers.
for the same total depth, the maximum transport of mucus takes place when the thickness of the mucus layer is equal to that of the serous layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mucus transport increases with increase in the porosity of cilia bed, pressure gradient, and the velocity due to cilia tips and decreases with increase in the viscosity of the mucus and serous layer fluid.

the transport of seros-mucus mixture in the human trachia is a function of the pressure drop, mucus viscosity and mucus elasticity, the velocity generated at cilia tips, porosity of the cilia bed and the thickness of serous fluid layer.

the transport of sero-mucus mixture is maximum for given pressure drop, cilia velocity, porosity and serous fluid viscosity when the thickness of serous layer is such that its thickness is equal to the sum of the thicknesses of the mucus and the porous bed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mucus transport can be enhanced by increasing the porosity parameter and cilia beating velocity.
the mucus transport is not affected significantly by the change of mucus viscosity.
the mucus transport is not only dependent on the properties of the serous fluid layer and mucus but also on the properties of cilia and mucus-air interface.
